notes: All 54 answers are YES. Close calls: (1) Q-T1-CUSTOMER-REFUND: the subject 'Customer refund for returned order items' narrows to 'items', while CR-2 concerns the delivery charge. I judged the subject to name the refund given on a return, so CR-2 is still about it. (2) Q-T1-PICKUP, Q-T1-WEIGHT and Q-T1-SELLER-LIMIT: the subjects contain 'cut-off' or 'limit', which appear in the question's dimension list. I answered YES because the question's test is that every proposition in the full sealed inventory is about the subject, and here it is (the cut-off or limit is the whole governed concern). A stricter reading, where any subject naming a limit or cut-off fails, would turn these three to NO. (3) Q-T1-NONOP-ORION and Q-T2-NONOP-ORION: the non_operative sentences are worked examples (J-8, Q-40) that restate specific cases of H-2/H-3/H-4. I treated specific instances as not stating the general sealed propositions, and each of those propositions is stated by a normative sentence in the accounting. (4) Q-T2-DISP-H-T9: one listed proposition (P4) covers both H-4 and H-5 with a single ASSERT_CLAIM. Nothing in the question forbids one listed proposition representing two sealed ones. (5) Q-T1-NONOP-CORE/JOBS/LARGE and Q-T2-NONOP-CORE/JOBS/LARGE: these are YES because non_operative is empty, so there was nothing to check.
